topic: Bedrock Induction Ratio κ = 1.677 (PRED-KAPPA-001) — verification of ISS-2855 + ISS-2856 patches (qid=539)
our_argument_summary: WIN-058b: κ = 1.677 nT/μGal is a post-hoc ratio from one extreme event (Oct 2003 G5), not a dome-derived prediction; the r = 0.992 correlation is consistent with shared electromagnetic forcing during G5 storms; numbering collides with the θ = −lonE WIN-058 entry. Verdict: Not Demonstrated.

code_analysis_tags.monitoring_evidence: No monitor.py path detected for the bedrock-κ claim. code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Standard physics does not name a 'bedrock-induction coupling constant' κ between magnetic and gravity residuals. (Standard physics DOES explain the observed correlation as shared electromagnetic forcing during G5 storms — but that is a critique of the dome's interpretation, not an existing standard-physics analog of κ.)
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: The 10.9/6.5 = 1.677 ratio is extracted from one observed event (October 2003 G5 storm, Dst = -383 nT). The 'prediction' is the measured value restated. detail_evidence ¶1 explicitly: 'A ratio extracted from one event is a measurement, not a prediction.'
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: detail_evidence ¶1 verbatim: 'No equation in the dome model derives κ = 1.677 ... from the disc radius (20,015 km), firmament height (9,086 km), or any other structural parameter.' Tag holds.

holes_found.description: Cross-surface r-threshold asymmetry NOT fully closed by ISS-2855. ISS-2855 tightened the new κ-cluster cross-reference paragraph in detail_evidence (paragraph 7) from 'r > 0.96 from shared forcing alone' to 'r ≈ 0.99 (mean 0.990, 90% CI: 0.985–0.994) from shared forcing alone, per the existing detail prose'. That patch is clean within detail_evidence. HOWEVER three sibling surfaces retain the looser 'r > 0.96' threshold: (1) WIN-058b.finding (the summary table row — high-visibility, what most readers see first) reads 'Monte Carlo shows shared electromagnetic forcing produces r > 0.96 at physically realistic SNR'; (2) WIN-058b.tldr_evidence (the collapsed pre-expand TLDR) reads 'Monte Carlo shows any two sensors sharing a G5 storm driver produce r > 0.96 at physically realistic SNR'; (3) sections.part6.html §6.14 storm-corollary subsection reads 'our Monte Carlo simulation (documented in WIN-058b detail) finds r > 0.96 from shared forcing alone'. Surface (3) is the worst of the three because it explicitly says 'documented in WIN-058b detail' — but WIN-058b detail now actually documents r ≈ 0.99 (mean 0.990, 90% CI: 0.985–0.994). A careful reader cross-clicking from §6.14 will see §6.14 attribute a threshold to WIN-058b that WIN-058b no longer carries. The c5 review's hole[2] recommendation explicitly named all surfaces (option a: 'tighten the cross-reference paragraph (and the matching §6.14 sentence) to match the actual Monte Carlo result') — the decider patched the cross-reference paragraph but not the matching §6.14 sentence, summary-row finding, or TLDR. Note this is consistent-direction-weaker, not contradictory — r ≈ 0.99 implies r > 0.96 — so the verdict is unchanged and the argument is not weakened to a reader who reads only one surface. Severity moderate because the §6.14 misattribution is verifiable inconsistency, not just stylistic divergence.
holes_found.recommendation: Propagate ISS-2855 tightening to the three remaining surfaces. Edits (single-line each): (a) WIN-058b.finding: 'r > 0.96 at physically realistic SNR' → 'r ≈ 0.99 (mean 0.990, 90% CI: 0.985–0.994) at physically realistic SNR'. (b) WIN-058b.tldr_evidence: 'r > 0.96 at physically realistic SNR' → 'r ≈ 0.99 at physically realistic SNR' (CI omitted in TLDR for brevity). (c) sections.part6.html §6.14: 'our Monte Carlo simulation (documented in WIN-058b detail) finds r > 0.96 from shared forcing alone' → 'our Monte Carlo simulation (documented in WIN-058b detail) finds r ≈ 0.99 (mean 0.990, 90% CI: 0.985–0.994) from shared forcing alone'. Single file each — pure text replacements. Note this re-opens the ISS-1988 (closed 2026-05-12) softening rationale, which deliberately removed the methodological-citation burden by going to r > 0.96; closing this hole means accepting that the WIN-058b Monte Carlo prose itself constitutes the methodology citation. That is defensible — the detail prose specifies τ = 30s, N = 1,620 samples, SNR = 10 with full assumption disclosure — but the closure rationale should be recorded so a future curmudgeon doesn't re-open ISS-1988.

The verdict (Not Demonstrated) and the underlying scientific argument (post-hoc one-event ratio, no dome-geometry derivation, expected shared-forcing correlation) are unaffected — this is a hygiene finding, not a verdict-relevant defect.

deeper_analysis: Verification pass for qid=539 (target_id WIN-058b, class=verification, pushed_at 2026-06-18T02:15:50Z). Phase 1 verify-mode handoff (PROP-038) gates fail (c5 had 4 holes, one major), so this stayed in main-curmudgeon scope; that classification was correct because the c5 unpatched holes needed adversarial follow-through. Adversarial pass found that the two qid=539 patches (ISS-2855 + ISS-2856) landed clean within their stated scope but ISS-2855's scope was narrower than the c5 hole[2] recommendation called for — see c6 hole[0]. The c5 hole[0] (major) and hole[1] (minor) were independently closed by a separate decider self-apply (commit 00e52de, ISS-2853 + ISS-2854) ~16 hours earlier; all four c5 findings are now fully or substantially addressed. Adversarial counter-consideration on c6 hole[0] severity: a dome defender would not weaponize this — they would call it stylistic tightening rather than a fact issue (r ≈ 0.99 ⇒ r > 0.96 is logically consistent, just stronger). That is fair. The severity-moderate classification is driven by the §6.14 misattribution specifically ('documented in WIN-058b detail' now claims a threshold WIN-058b detail no longer carries), which is verifiable cross-surface inconsistency a careful reader will catch — not by the summary-row weaker-framing issue per se. If you remove the §6.14 misattribution, the finding falls to minor.
